add_room.title: Room — step 1 of 2
add_room.description:
**Room step 1 of 2.** Top: what the remote shows for this room. Below: what **Room Off** does, in four boxes.

**Room Off right now:**
{plan}

Everything an activity in this room switches on (TV, amp, projector …) is always in **Turns off**, unless you put it under **Never touched**.

data_description.lights: Dimmable lights get a slider on the remote; switches and relays are on / off.

data.off_ask: Ask first on the remote (Room Off sheet)

data_description.off_ask: On: tapping Room Off on the screen shows what will turn off, with on/off toggles for the **Your choice** items. The remote's power key never asks — it turns off straight away with the defaults below.

data_description.off_extra: Besides everything the activities switched on: fans, a heater, a TV that isn't in an activity. A **button**, script or scene here is pressed / run (e.g. a projector-off button).
data_description.off_action: A script, scene or automation that runs last, after everything is off.

your_choice.name: 🟠 Your choice — the client decides on the remote

data.off_choice_on: Other devices — left on by default

data_description.off_lights_mode: **Always off** / **Never** don't ask. The two **Ask** options show a toggle on the Room Off sheet, set the way you choose here.
data_description.off_choice_off: Shown on the Room Off sheet, switched ON so they turn off unless the client flips it.
data_description.off_choice_on: Shown on the Room Off sheet, switched OFF so they stay on unless the client flips it.

stays_on.name: 🔵 Stays on for a bit, then switches off

data_description.off_delayed: They stay on after Room Off and switch off by themselves (an amp running down, a passage light to walk out by). A **button** here is pressed when its time is up. Starting an activity that uses one cancels its timer. Timers survive a restart.
data_description.off_delay_minutes: For all of them; after Submit, the next page lets you give each device its own time.

data_description.off_never: Even when an activity switched it on — e.g. a pool pump, a gate light, the amp in another zone.

add_activity.title: Activity — step 1 of 5: devices
add_activity.description:
**Activity step 1 of 5: the devices.**

• **Source**: what you watch or listen to (Apple TV, DStv, Spotify). The D-pad, OK and play keys control it.
• **Volume device**: what the volume keys control (the amp / soundbar / TV).
• **Also turn on**: everything else that must come on — projector, screen, subwoofer. Network devices, plugs / relays, or an IR / RF **button** that switches one on.

Next page: which input each one goes to, and how button-controlled devices are switched off.

data.name: Activity name
data.devices: Also turn on (projector, amp, screen … or a button that turns one on)
data.power_on: Extra action when the activity starts (optional)
data.ir_device: IR device (sent by the remote's own IR)
data.switch_mode: Coming from another activity of the same type

data_description.volume: Volume, mute and the volume rocker go here. Leave empty to use the source.
data_description.dpad: A remote entity — Apple TV, Android TV, Roku, Samsung, LG or a Broadlink/IR remote.
data_description.command_set: Which command names the navigation remote understands.
data_description.devices: Switched on when the activity starts. A button / script is pressed. At Room Off (or when the next activity doesn't use them) they're switched off — a device switched on by a button needs its **turn off with** command on the next page, otherwise Home Assistant can't switch it off.
data_description.power_on: A script or scene to run as well. For lights, delays and more, use the next pages.
data_description.logo: Already have the image in Home Assistant? e.g. `/local/netflix.png`. Leave both empty for the Watch / Listen icon.
data_description.logo_upload: Pick an image from your computer or phone (PNG or JPG; square looks best). Shown on the remote's Watch / Listen picker.
data_description.now_playing: The title and picture on the remote's Watch screen come from the source. Android TV Remote only reports the app, not the title — pick the TV's **Google Cast** entity here (or Plex, Kodi, Spotify) and the remote shows its title and picture instead. Leave empty to use the source.
data_description.ir_device: Its up / down / OK / back / volume / play codes go out of the remote's IR blaster. Keys without a code still use the navigation remote above.
data_description.switch_mode: E.g. Netflix → Apple TV while watching. **Sources only**: missing devices power on and inputs change; the lights and scene stay as they are. Pressing an activity that's already playing never re-runs anything.
data_description.icon: Shown on the Watch / Listen picker when the activity has no logo of its own (e.g. a realistic Blu-ray player or satellite dish). An uploaded or typed logo wins.

edit_activity.description:
**Activity step 1 of 5: the devices.**

• **Source**: what you watch or listen to (Apple TV, DStv, Spotify). The D-pad, OK and play keys control it.
• **Volume device**: what the volume keys control (the amp / soundbar / TV).
• **Also turn on**: everything else that must come on — projector, screen, subwoofer. Network devices, plugs / relays, or an IR / RF **button** that switches one on.

Next page: which input each one goes to, and how button-controlled devices are switched off.

buttons.title: {activity} — step 5 of 5: buttons
buttons.description:
What the remote's buttons do while this activity runs. Leave any empty.

• **Custom 1–3**: three buttons on the remote's screen — give each a name and an action.
• **Red / Green / Blue / Yellow**: the coloured hard keys (their names show at the bottom of the screen).

An **action** can be a script, scene, button or automation (it runs), or a light / switch / fan (it toggles on and off). Tip: an automation runs its actions only — its trigger and conditions are skipped. To toggle a light, pick the light itself.

Not working? The room's activity entity in Home Assistant shows **last_button**: what was pressed and what happened.

sources.title: {activity} — step 2 of 5: inputs, volume and power off

data.source_input: Source — app or input to open (empty = leave it)
data.input: Volume device — input to switch to (empty = stays on whatever it's on)
data.start_volume: Volume device — set the volume to (empty = don't change)
data.input_delay: Wait after switching on, before inputs and volume
data.sound_mode: Volume device — sound mode (empty = leave it)
data.sound_mode_delay: Wait after the input change, before the sound mode

data_description.input: Only if the amp / soundbar also switches the picture or sound source, e.g. a Denon set to GAME or TV AUDIO. Leave empty if it should just stay where it is.
data_description.start_volume: 0–100 %. Set when the activity starts. Leave empty to keep the current volume.
data_description.input_delay: Gives the amp, projector and TV time to wake up after they're switched on. If everything was already on, inputs switch straight away. A device already on the right input is left alone.
data_description.sound_mode: Whatever this amp / soundbar offers: Stereo, Mono, Direct, Dolby Surround, Movie … Not listed? Type it exactly as Home Assistant shows it and press Enter. Left alone if it's already on it.
data_description.sound_mode_delay: Most amps ignore a sound mode while they're still changing input. With the 7 s wake-up wait and 5 s here, the sound mode goes in about 12 s after the activity starts.

actions.title: {activity} — step 3 of 4: what else happens
actions.description:
Optional — leave it all empty if the devices on step 1 are enough.

• **Turn off when the activity starts**: things that may be on but must be off (room lights, another TV).
• **Turn on for a few seconds, then off**: e.g. a light while everything powers up, or a screen-drop relay.
Both get their own time per device on the next page.

• **When the activity starts / ends**: anything else, built like an HA script (dim lights to 20 %, close curtains, wait 2 s …).

data.stop_actions: When the activity ends (switching away or Room Off)
data.turn_off_on_end: Turn off everything the start steps turned on when the activity ends
data.off_on_start: Turn off when the activity starts
data.pulse: Turn on for a few seconds, then off again

data_description.turn_off_on_end: Lights, switches and players used in the start steps go off at Room Off or when you switch to an activity that doesn't use them. Music is paused first.
data_description.off_on_start: Things that may already be on but must be off for this activity (a light, another TV, a fan). A button / script here is pressed instead. Each gets its own delay on the next page — 0 is straight away.
data_description.pulse: Each comes on when the activity starts and switches itself off after its own number of seconds (next page) — e.g. a light that flashes on while everything powers up, or a screen-drop relay.

remote_settings.title: Remote settings
remote_settings.description: How the remote itself behaves. Clients can change brightness, Wi-Fi, the logo clock and a few more on the remote (swipe down from the top); installer settings there are behind the PIN below.

data.splash_seconds: Show the logo at start-up for
data.charging_screen: Show the charging screen when the remote is put on charge
data.clock_after: Show the clock after (no key pressed)
data.pickup: Wake the screen when the remote is picked up
data.key_REWIND_action: ⏪ key — action (when set to Run an action)
data.key_PLAY_action: ⏵ key — action (when set to Run an action)
data.key_STOP_action: ⏹ key — action (when set to Run an action)
data.key_FASTFORWARD_action: ⏩ key — action (when set to Run an action)

data_description.logo: e.g. `/local/logo.png`. Clear it (and don't upload) for the built-in A&R Smart Home logo.
data_description.splash_seconds: 0 turns the start-up logo off. Note: Android's own boot animation before the app starts can't be changed without rooting the remote.
data_description.pickup: Auto works on any remote: it keeps the motion sensor running while the screen is off (uses some battery). Battery saver only uses low-power sensors, which many remotes don't have. Lifting it off the charger always wakes it. The **Pick-up sensor** entity shows what the remote is using.
data_description.pickup_sensitivity: High wakes on a gentle lift; Low needs a firmer pick-up (fewer accidental wakes from bumps).
data_description.logo_upload: Pick an image from your computer or phone. A PNG with a transparent background looks best on the dark screen. Leave empty to keep the current logo.
data_description.clock: Your logo as a clock face. On the charger, the screen stays on and the clock appears instead of going dark; any key or tap goes back. Always also shows it off the charger (keeps the screen on — uses a lot of battery).
data_description.installer_pin: Protects **Installer settings** on the remote's pull-down panel (Android settings, restart, updates). Leave empty to keep the current PIN. Only a hash is stored.
data_description.clock_x: Leave both empty for automatic (the A&R logo's circle, or the middle of another logo). For the A&R logo the circle is at 50.4 % across, 37.1 % down.
data_description.key_REWIND: What the four media keys do. By default each opens the screen its icon shows. **Play controls** is the old behaviour (rewind / play / stop / forward on the source). **Run an action** runs the script, scene or button picked below it, on any screen.
data_description.clock_for: How long the logo clock keeps the screen on before it goes dark like normal (also on the charger). Any key, a tap or picking the remote up brings it back.

copy_activity.title: Copy an activity
copy_activity.description: Makes a copy with the same devices, inputs, start/end steps and buttons. Next you can change what's different, like the name, logo and the app on the source.

data.name: Name of the copy
data.room: Room (leave empty for the same room)

room_timers.title: {room} — step 2 of 2: Room Off timers
room_timers.description: How many minutes each device keeps running after Room Off before it switches itself off. A device switched on by a button uses its **turn off with** command (set on the activity's step 2). Timers survive a Home Assistant restart. Starting an activity that uses the device cancels its timer.

timers.title: {activity} — step 3b: timers
timers.description: One time per device, in seconds. **Turn off after**: how long after the activity starts it goes off (0 = straight away). **Stay on for**: how long the device stays on before it switches itself off.

start_steps.title: {activity} — step 3 of 5: when it starts
start_steps.description:
Runs like a script the moment the activity starts — top to bottom, each step: **devices → do → then wait**. The source, amp and projector from steps 1–2 switch on at the same time as step 1, and the remote is usable straight away while this runs.

Leave a step empty to skip it. A step with no devices but a wait is just a pause. Anything turned on here goes off at Room Off (unless the next page handles it).

data_description.entities: One or more — lights, switches, TV, plug, button, script, automation …
data_description.level: Only for **Dim to %**: brightness (lights), position (blinds), volume (players).

end_steps.title: {activity} — step 4 of 5: when it's switched off
end_steps.description:
Runs like a script at **Room Off** (or the power key), and when you switch to another activity — top to bottom, each step: **devices → do → then wait**. E.g. dim the downlights to 60 %, press screen up, wait 25 s, run the projector-off automation.

The source, amp and projector still switch off as set on step 2. Devices you put here are left to these steps (Room Off doesn't switch them off itself). Starting an activity again stops these steps where they are.

data_description.entities: One or more — lights, switches, TV, plug, button, script, automation …
data_description.level: Only for **Dim to %**: brightness (lights), position (blinds), volume (players).

data.stop_actions: Also run when it's switched off
data.turn_off_on_end: Room Off also turns off everything the start steps turned on

ir_devices.title: IR devices
ir_devices.description:
The remote has its own IR blaster. Add each IR-controlled device here (TV, amp, projector, aircon) with its codes, then pick it on an activity under **IR device**: its D-pad, volume and play keys then go out of the remote's IR straight away, no Wi-Fi needed.

Home Assistant can send them too: `remote.send_command` on the remote's **IR blaster** entity, with `device` and `command`.

data_description.new_name: Only for a new device, e.g. Samsung TV or Lounge amp.

ir_edit.title: IR codes — {device}
ir_edit.description:
One code per line: **name: code**. Names the remote's keys use: up, down, left, right, ok, back, menu, home, volume_up, volume_down, mute, channel_up, channel_down, play_pause (or play), stop, rewind, fast_forward. Add any others you like (power, power_on, hdmi1 …) for scripts.

Codes can be:
• Pronto hex: `0000 006D 0022 0002 0157 00AC …`
• Broadlink learned code (base64): `JgBQAAABJ5MU…`
• NEC: `nec:0x04:0x08` (address : command)
• Samsung: `samsung:0x07:0x02`
• Raw: `raw:38000:9000,4500,560,560,…`

Clear all the codes to delete this device.

light_names.title: {room} — light names on the remote
light_names.description: Each box is a light in this room, labelled with its Home Assistant name. Type the name you want on the remote (e.g. **Downlights**, **Cove**, **Pool light**). Leave a box empty to use the Home Assistant name.

menu_options.edit_activity: ① Devices — what turns on, logo, remote
menu_options.sources: ② Sources — inputs, volume, sound mode, off commands

home_icons.title: Home screen icons
home_icons.description:
**Look** sets the whole remote: **Classic** is the flat dark look with amber; **Residence** puts a photo behind glass cards, with champagne highlights, lighter lettering and its own TV, speaker, bulb, aircon and blinds icons (the 4C Dash look). **Background** is the photo for Residence.

The room's home page on the remote: **Round** puts each icon in a lit bubble; **Icons only** shows just the icon and its name.

For each icon you can pick one from the **built-in library** ({count} icons, realistic and line), upload your own image (its plain background is cut away on the remote), or type an address such as `/local/icons/tv.png`. Your own image wins over a built-in icon; leave all three empty for the standard icon.

data_description.look: Works with both Round and Icons only below. In Residence, Round is a glass ring and Icons only adds a soft light behind what is on.
data_description.background: Only used by the Residence look. The remote darkens it so the icons and names stay readable.
data_description.home_style: Built-in icons take the accent colour when active. Your own images are shown as they are.
data_description.icon_set: Used for every icon you don't pick below. **Realistic**: full-colour TV, speaker, bulb, aircon, blinds, star, red power button. **Line**: white outline icons that turn amber when active.
